title: A constructible abelian sheaf killed by n is a constructible sheaf of Z/n-modules
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $n\ge1$ an integer and $C$ a constructible abelian sheaf on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf] with $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_C=0$. Let $\tilde C$ be $C$ with its unique structure of sheaf of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules extending its abelian structure [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules], an object of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z/n)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\tilde C$ is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$), and every stratification witnessing the constructibility of $C$ witnesses that of $\tilde C$. (Ingredients: the module inverse image along an immersion $\iota_k$ has the abelian inverse image as underlying abelian sheaf (cf. [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] (1)), and is killed by $n$; a finite abelian group $A$ with $(\iota_k^{-1}C)|_{V}\cong\underline A$ on a nonempty $V$ has $nA=0$ ($A$ is a stalk), so it is a finite $\mathbf Z/n$-module, and the constant abelian sheaf $\underline A$ is the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules with value $A$, both being the sheafification of the same presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; an isomorphism of abelian sheaves between sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules is $\mathbf Z/n$-linear by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] (3). The converse also holds and is not part of this node. This is the general-scheme form of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion-modules-agree], which states it for curves.)

source.place: Definition 03RW (2) and (3), line 11672, read with Definition 03RU, line 9917; Stacks passes between the two notions without comment (e.g. Lemma 09Z7 (2)/(3), line 13028). Not stated as a lemma in Stacks; agent-formulated.

proof.text: By the hypothesis $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_C=0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] (2), the abelian sheaf $C$ has exactly one sheaf-of-$(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules structure extending its addition; denote the resulting module sheaf by $\tilde C$. Clause (1) of that node says that the underlying abelian sheaf of every such module is killed by $n$, and clause (3) says that every abelian-sheaf isomorphism between two such module sheaves is $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-linear. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf of $\tilde C$ is exactly $C$ and the coefficient structure is fixed for the rest of the proof.

source.place: Definition 03RW (2) and (3), together with the coefficient passage used in the proof of Theorem 03SC; the module construction is formalized by the cited node

proof.text: Fix any stratification $(\iota_k:Z_k\to T)_{k<r}$ witnessing constructibility of $C$ in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. Its strata are constructible, and on each $Z_k$ there are an etale cover $v_{ki}:U_{ki}\to Z_k$, finite abelian groups $A_{ki}$ and abelian-sheaf isomorphisms $(\iota_k^{-1}C)|_{U_{ki}}\cong\underline{A_{ki}}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (1),(2), the module inverse image of $\tilde C$ along $\iota_k$ has underlying abelian sheaf $\iota_k^{-1}C$, up to canonical isomorphism. Apply the same comparison also along each $v_{ki}$: the underlying sheaf of the restricted module sheaf $H_{ki}=v_{ki}^{-1}\iota_k^{-1}\tilde C$ is canonically $(\iota_k^{-1}C)|_{U_{ki}}$. It is killed by $n$, by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] on $U_{ki}$. This uses the constant-ring module pullback, not tensoring along an unrelated coefficient map.

source.place: Definition 03RU and Definition 03RW (2),(3), line 11672; inverse-image compatibility is the sheaf-theoretic pullback used in Lemma 03Q1

proof.text: Discard the empty $U_{ki}$; the remaining etale family has the same union of images and is still a cover (if $Z_k$ is empty it is the empty covering). On a remaining $U=U_{ki}\ne\emptyset$, choose $u\in U$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of its residue field, which exists by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is a geometric point $\bar u$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The abelian isomorphism in step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] identify $A_{ki}$ with the stalk of the underlying abelian sheaf of $H_{ki}$ at $\bar u$. This stalk is killed by $n$: in the colimit defining it [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], every representative section $s$ satisfies $ns=0$ by step 2, so its germ satisfies $n[s]=[ns]=0$. The isomorphism therefore implies $na=0$ for every $a\in A_{ki}$.

source.place: Definitions 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) and 03RW (definition-constructible), parts (2),(3); constant stalk identification: Lemma 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact), part (2), and Definition 040R (definition-stalk)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n] (1), give $A_{ki}$ its $\mathbf Z/n$-module structure $\bar a\cdot x=ax$. It remains a finite set. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying] on $U_{ki}$ with $R=\mathbf Z/n$ and $M=A_{ki}$: the constant module sheaf $\underline{A_{ki}}^{\mathbf Z/n}$ has underlying abelian sheaf canonically isomorphic to $\underline{A_{ki}}$. Composing this comparison with the trivialization from step 2 gives an abelian-sheaf isomorphism from the underlying sheaf of $H_{ki}$ to that of $\underline{A_{ki}}^{\mathbf Z/n}$. By clause (3) and the final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules], it and its inverse are $(\mathbf Z/n)_{U_{ki}}$-linear. Thus $H_{ki}\cong\underline{A_{ki}}^{\mathbf Z/n}$ as module sheaves. Every stratum consequently has an etale trivializing cover with finite module values.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), applied to constant module presheaves; Definitions 03RU and 03RW (2),(3) in etale-cohomology.tex

proof.text: The same strata $(\iota_k)$ therefore satisfy condition (a) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] because their underlying subsets were already constructible, and condition (b) because step 4 supplies an etale cover on each stratum by constant sheaves of finite $\mathbf Z/n$-modules. Hence $\tilde C$ is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules, and the argument used the originally chosen stratification without changing it.
